visible.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cv2' while deploying streamlit app
visible.body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Just doing random app using cv2 and streamlit when i tried to deploy following error occurs.kindly help me to solve this error!!1

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from PIL import Image
import cv2
import numpy as np

select=st.selectbox("pick",["camera","upload image"])
if select=="camera":
    cam=st.camera_input("capture a photo")
    if cam is not None:
        file_bytes = np.asarray(bytearray(cam.read()), dtype=np.uint8)
        opencv_image = cv2.imdecode(file_bytes, 1)
        st.image(opencv_image,channel="RGB")

else:
    uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a image file", type=["jpg","png"])
    if uploaded_file is not None:
        file_bytes = np.asarray(bytearray(uploaded_file.read()), dtype=np.uint8)
        opencv_image1= cv2.imdecode(file_bytes, 1)
        st.image(opencv_image1,channels="BGR")
```

hypotheses: Requirements file not discovered or deployment uses another revision.
OpenCV installation failed or was installed in another environment.

missing_info.item: Actual committed dependency filename/path and successful build installation log
missing_info.why: Distinguishes a singular filename, undiscovered requirements file, failed install or stale deployment.

missing_info.item: Interpreter/environment used to install and run cv2

acceptable_next_steps: Ask whether the actual file is requirements.txt and inspect the deployed commit/build log; do not assume the heading typo is definitive.
Verify OpenCV import with the runtime interpreter and compare its package installation with the build environment.
must_not: Tell the user simply to add opencv-python-headless without acknowledging it is already listed.
Treat missing libGL as established from ModuleNotFoundError alone.
Escalate as a confirmed Streamlit bug.
gold.reference: Maintainer: use opencv-python-headless; not a Streamlit bug.
gold.review_reason: The visible report ALREADY lists opencv-python-headless. Its heading says requirement.txt (singular). Ask/check the actual filename, deployed revision, install log and interpreter; adding the same dependency blindly does not discriminate causes. Guidance is acceptable if it explicitly addresses this discrepancy.

acceptable_next_steps: Recommend adding opencv-python-headless to requirements.txt (KB articles)
